## Context / Problem
`scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` prints only aggregate counts on a failing check (e.g. `active=41 new=2 increased=1 stale=7`). It never names the offending symbols, their files, current McCabe scores, or the baseline ceiling/threshold they breached. Diagnosing a CI failure (e.g. Gerrit run 32914110990) currently requires a separate local no-cache Ruff census plus manual baseline comparison — especially poor in resource-constrained CI-only workflows. Split out from bug 0ab0-6754-cc72-4d8c, which the operator classified not_a_bug: the terse output is the documented, --help-surfaced, unit-tested contract (module 'Exit-code contract' docstring + test_help_documents_contracts), so this is an approved ENHANCEMENT, not a defect.

## Plan
- Preserve the existing compact counter summary line (`active=<A> new=<N> increased=<I> stale=<S>`) byte-for-byte so anything parsing it today keeps working.
- On a FAILING `--check` (new>0 or increased>0), after the summary emit additive, deterministic per-symbol detail lines:
  - one line per `new` symbol: `  new       <file>::<symbol> score=<n> threshold=<15>`.
  - one line per `increased` symbol: `  increased <file>::<symbol> score=<n> ceiling=<c>`.
- Detail lines are stable-sorted (by key) within each group.
- Keep passing and stale-only output compact — NO detail lines when there is no regression.
- Do NOT alter the pass/fail gate logic (has_regression / exit codes) — formatting only over already-computed data; scanner/gate runtime unchanged.
- Update the module 'Exit-code contract' docstring accordingly.
- Add focused unit coverage for detail values, ordering, and absence-on-pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A failing `--check` names every `new` symbol with file::symbol, current score, and the allowed threshold.
- [x] A failing `--check` names every `increased` symbol with file::symbol, current score, and baseline ceiling.
- [x] Detail lines are stable-sorted and appear together with the existing summary line, which is unchanged.
- [x] A passing or stale-only check retains compact output with no violation detail lines.
- [x] Pass/fail gate logic and exit codes are unchanged.
- [x] Focused tests plus `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
